Our 5e campaign worlds tend to be sandboxes built on hexmaps, and our group always ends up doing a lot of wilderness adventuring once they hit level 5 or so. In AD&D, this style of play is accommodated by a line in each monster's stat block called % In Lair. The idea is that if a monster is encountered randomly in the wilderness -- or perhaps even in the dungeon -- there is a chance that it happens to be at home. Uncovering a monster lair is great because that's where the treasure is. It is also dangerous business because you tend to encounter a greater number of monsters than you might find wandering out in the woods.

To facilitate this style of play in 5e, I constructed this table. The % Lair values here were harvested from original AD&D sources (Monster Manual, Fiend Folio, Monster Manual II, adventure modules, Dragon Magazine articles, and OSRIC) as much as possible. When such sources were unavailable, I went to the original D&D boxed set and supplements. The % In Lair statistic was unfortunately abandoned in Basic D&D and in 2nd edition AD&D.

It was a fun project to hunt down as many entries as possible, but a number of the entries in the 5e Monster Manual were sourced from non-AD&D editions of the game, and many from Fifth Edition Foes were originally written for Swords and Wizardry, which also omits this statistic. In these cases, I made up a value by comparing the monster in question to one for which I had the statistic already.

I hope you are able to find this pdf to be as fun and as useful as I have.
